Hey, can you sort out the art board for me. Domino has been dead since August and nobody has properly been through it since, so it is still carrying a pile of tickets from a game we are not shipping any more. Start with the honest count: how many tickets are genuinely still open on it, not just what the filter tells you, how many of those have not moved in the last twelve months, and how the open ones split across the people holding them. I want that split by owner, including how many sit with nobody at all. Some of what looks open is already finished and never got marked. Anything still sitting in review that the record shows was completed should be closed off properly, and tell me how many you closed that way. Then take what is genuinely left and go through it one by one, checking whether anything anywhere says the work is finished, a message or a commit, and tell me what you found for each. Close the ones you find something for and only those. Where there is nothing, say so and leave it open. Whoever is sitting on the most of the stale ones has clearly stopped working them, so pull all of their open tickets onto my name, along with anything that has nobody on it at all, and tell me who it was and how many tickets end up on me. Then send Leonard the numbers: the open count, the stale count, the split by owner, how many you closed as already finished, what you found behind each of the rest, and who I took work off and how many landed on me.

## Hint
Do not take the board's own state labels at face value. Check what each record actually says before you decide whether something is still open.

Anything on that board that is actually Zombie work does not belong there, so flag it and say where it should live.

The playable ads people have been chasing us and nobody here has answered. Work out where that stands and raise a ticket so it stops getting dropped.

Do not put anything more on Marcus, he is buried in Zombie
I will check the Trello boards to
locate the art board and search for user information across Slack, Contacts, and Trello.

Prototype Requirements:
Art Team:
• 5 total unique monsters, 15 total
    ◦ 4 basic monsters with 3 color variants (12 total)
    ◦ 1 boss monster with 3 color variants (3 total)
• Basic animation suite
    ◦ Walking
    ◦ Idling
    ◦ Attacking
    ◦ Hit by object
    ◦ Death
• VFX
    ◦ Optimized object flight
        ▪︎ Size of object
        ▪︎ Spin
        ▪︎ Trajectory
    ◦ Ground effects
        ▪︎ Explosion
        ▪︎ Shock
        ▪︎ Freeze
        ▪︎ Poison
        ▪︎ Fire
    ◦ Boost VFX
        ▪︎ Instantly removes 1 set of items and throws it at zombies (Vacuum in Match Factory)
        ▪︎ VFX that throws items from the inventory back onto the board, either 1 or all
        ▪︎ VFX that freezes all monsters on screen for 10 seconds (new monsters can still spawn)
        ▪︎ Time extension - giant gust of air that blows all the zombies back by about a screen worth
• Objects
    ◦ 50-100 total objects. 50 good ones or 100 mediocre ones
    ◦ Each object should have color variants if allowed, 5 color variants minimum each. (Unless it's like a hamburger where variants are not really possible)
    ◦ Total is between 250-500 objects including variants
    ◦ Shape of object is most important (balanced object that looks uniform from all angles, tricky shaped objects, noisy objects, we need a variety)
    ◦ Color and texture of object is the next important factor (Couch cloth, wooden feel, metallic, bright colors, multi colors, we need a variety)
    ◦ Material, lighting and shadow also needs to be optimized
• UI
    ◦ Home screen
    ◦ Pre-level dialog for booster selection
    ◦ End game screen
    ◦ Leaderboards
    ◦ Live Ops icon and UI panels
Engineering:
• Core game functionality
• Bug free matching mechanism including inventory bar shuffling VFX (Adding items that already exist on bar, etc.)
• Single clickable items (In-game one click objects and power ups)
    ◦ Catapult - instantly matches a random set of item and throw it at zombies
    ◦ Rest is TBD
• Battlefield animations
• Life System
• Star System
• (Later version) Coin economy system
• (Later version) Shop and hard currency
• SFX system
    ◦ Individual object level sound effects
        ▪︎ Object thrown
        ▪︎ Object hitting monsters
        ▪︎ Object residual post impact (If any)
    ◦ Fall back sound settings if object level settings not present
        ▪︎ Object thrown - use default
        ▪︎ Object hit - Use item properties default sound (Shock, explosion, etc.) If multiple properties exist, play them all.
        ▪︎ Object residual post impact (No default needed, silent)
    ◦ Monster sounds
        ▪︎ Spawn (If not specified, default is silent)
            • Spawn sound play option toggle. (Play every spawn / Play only when same monster does not exist on board)
        ▪︎ Walking - ambient growl
            • Check all monsters on field, play a random ambient sound from one of the existing monsters every 5 seconds. Ignore monsters that does not have an ambient sound.
        ▪︎ Monster attack and hitting fence
        ▪︎ Monster death (Ability to set multiple and choose random)
        ▪︎ Monster being hit sound (If not specified, default is silent)
    ◦ Generic UI clicking sounds (We can use Domino Delights)
• Leaderboards (Sort by level completed lifetime AND/OR stars earned lifetime)
• 1 Live Ops feature (Some kind of level race TBD)
• In-Game boosts
    ◦ A boost that matches a set of item instantly and throws it at zombies
    ◦ A boost that shuffles the board (Fan)
    ◦ A boost that throws the last object on the inventory bar back on the board
    ◦ A boost that freezes all enemies on screen for 10 seconds.
• Optimized environment
    ◦ Gravity that makes sense
    ◦ Physics that allows some object motion when bumped
Backend:
• Level editor
    ◦ Star settings based on finish time. 1, 2, 3 stars. <X seconds = 3 stars, <Y = 2 stars, <Z = 1 star (any completion)
    ◦ Monster spawning
        ▪︎ Specify start/stop time for each monster track
        ▪︎ Frequency setting and spawn interval settings
    ◦ Item spawning
        ▪︎ Item counts for each difficulty (currently 2 difficulty allowed)
        ▪︎ Multi layer system, supports 6+ layers with grid of 6x6 (Should allow designers to change the grid shape)
        ▪︎ intra and inter layer shuffling
        ▪︎ Force bottom with toggle to ignore or accept intra layer shuffle
    ◦ In-game single click power up spawning
        ▪︎ Set type and quantity
        ▪︎ Set approximate location in object stack
            • Input is 0-100. 0 is bottom, 100 is top. A range input of 0-100 means power up is evenly distributed in all layers.
            • If multiple range selected for example 0-20, 80-100, power up will appear near bottom, and near top. Multi range possible 0-10, 35-45, 85-95.
            • If 100 is the only value, object is on very top. 0 means very bottom
            • Power ups are not affected by item spawning and shuffling rules.
    ◦ UI and organization
        ▪︎ Level can be named and position can be reshuffled easily.
        ▪︎ (Future version) allow multiple difficulty settings. Default = 1, additional settings are 2, 3, 4, 5+
            • Higher number = easier.
            • We have algo that decides what player start each one at, and how they step up and down.
            • Each difficulty number will have it's own setting of object quantity settings.
                ◦ So for example level 5, difficulty 1 will have 12 hotdogs, difficulty 2 will have 6, difficulty will have 3, and difficulty will have 0.
            • Level designers will "add" the additional difficulty settings. Every level starts with default 1 until designer adds other difficulty levels
        ▪︎ Unnumbered levels - These are levels to expand the content of the game that introduces new objects as they are released.
            • After the initial first 100 levels, every 50 levels a player finished will force an encounter of these unnumbered levels. We call them "pack levels" So after a player finishes level 150, the next level is a pack level. Then the numbering continues with level 151... 152... 153....
            • We insert these pack levels every 50 levels until we are out of pack levels.
            • If the player has unlocked all pack levels, and we release a new pack level one day via content expansion, the player will get the pack level IMMEDIATELY after they finish their first numbered level. And then after the pack level completion the numbering resumes from where we left off
            • It is likely we have to algorithmically generate some levels after a certain point, I don't believe all levels are deterministic

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

ComboTimeout2x4.5s3x4.25s......18x~0s

are copy pasted here for convenience and tracking purpose.

- [X] Oval Shaped Tiles - These are the only objects that players can drop in the entire game, any other objects are dropped or spawned onto the board by chance, or they appear through a user-initiated power-up.
- [X] Jumbo Tiles - These are large size tiles with 4 icons on them, the moment they hit the platform, the entire game board will shake, possibly sending objects into various pits.
- [X] Hero Tokens - These are the same as the main game, a material required for users to upgrade their character levels. They spawn by chance or appear as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Gold Tiles - These are the same as the main game, a tile that can be saved in a player’s inventory that can be used in the main Dominoes Delights game, they also appear by chance or as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Bomb Tiles - These spawn by % chance, the % chance is tweakable through hero levels from the main game. When a fire token is pushed into the bottom pit, a random bomb tile on the board explodes, blowing nearby pieces in all directions.
- [X] Fire Tokens - These spawn randomly whenever a bomb tile spawns. Bomb tiles and fire tokens effectively spawn as a pair on the board. When they are pushed into the bottom pit, they ignite a bomb tile on the game board.
- [X] Jumbo Tile Token - These are a token representation of the jumbo tile. When they are collected in the bottom pit, an actual jumbo tile will drop onto the board at the tile drop area. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Tile Shower Token - These are a token representation of the tile shower power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a tile shower happens. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Castle Walls Token - These are a token representation of the castle walls power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a pair of castle walls rises for a brief period on the left and right pit of the game board. The duration of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Gems - Hard currency of the game, appears by chance.
- [X] Stars - Upgrading currency of the game, appears by chance.

  * **One-time offer**
  * **Must be purchased to unlock the next offer**
* **Provisions Pack**
  * **Trigger:** Shown only **after Day Zero Pack is purchased**
  * **Availability:** Live for **4 days**

* **Strategist’s Pack**
  * **Trigger:** Shown only **after Provisions Pack is purchased**
  * **Availability:** Live for **5 days**
  * **One-time offer**

---

### **Shared Offer Behavior:**

* Only **one offer is active at a time** per user.
* All offers appear under the **same HUD icon (top-right corner)**.
* Pop-up animation, tracking, and timer logic should reuse the **existing functionality from Domino Delights.**

---

**Notes:**

* Offers must expire cleanly if the user does not purchase within the time limit.

* Ensure purchase status is persistently stored and respected across sessions.

Since we're establishing a **baseline with no pity mechanic**, we'll first analyze **win rates without any pity adjustments** and then optimize the **base pity mechanic**.

## **1. Test Conditions**

We will run simulations for **Chapter 5, Levels 1-15**, under different **pity mechanic configurations**.

### **Baseline Condition (No Pity Mechanic)**

* **Goal:** Establish the **raw win rate** without any pity influence.
* **Test Runs:** **7,500 bot plays (500 per level)**.
* **Other Constants:**
  * **Character:** Sophie (Level 10)
  * **No adjustments** to **unique symbols, chops, or starting hand tiles**.
  * **No win streaks, no pre-level boosters**.

#### **Metrics to Record:**

* **Attempts**
* **Losses**
* **Avg Win Rate**
* **Avg Handtiles Left When Won**
* **How Many Board Tiles Left When Lost**
* **# of Tiles on the Board at Start**
* **# of Tiles on the Starting Draw Pile**
* **Avg Additional Tiles to finish the level when lost**

### **Test Variations for Base Pity Mechanic**

Once the baseline is set, we will optimize these **base pity mechanic parameters**:

```
{0.0f, 0.1f, 0.16f, 0.26f, 0.41f, 0.66f, 1.0f}
```

* **Goal:** Determine the best sequence of pity activations.
* **Variations:** Adjust **each probability in the range** to fine-tune the balance.

#### **Test Cases**

Each bot will:

1. **Play without a pity mechanic (baseline test).**
2. **Play with different base pity mechanic variations.**
3. **Log key win/loss metrics.**

---

## **2. Optimization Strategy**

Once data is collected:

1. **Compare baseline win rates to pity-adjusted win rates.**
2. **Use Bayesian Optimization** to find the best pity mechanic activation sequence.
3. \*\*Validate the final settings in a second simulation batch.

---

## **3. Running Bayesian Optimization to Determine Optimal Pity Mechanic Parameters**

Since **Bayesian Optimization (BO)** is well-suited for optimizing **multi-variable functions** with expensive evaluations (such as bot simulations), we will use it to **find the best pity mechanic parameters** for *Domino Delights*.

### **1. Problem Setup**

We need to **find the optimal pity mechanic settings** that:

✅ Keep the **win rate in the target range (based on the level's base win rate)**.

✅ Ensure a **near-miss experience** by adjusting **pity activation probabilities**.

### **Parameters to Optimize**

Bayesian Optimization will **fine-tune the pity probabilities**:

| **Pull Number** | **Current Pity Activation (Baseline)** | **Optimization Range** |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **1st** | 0.0f | Fixed (No pity on first pull) |
| **2nd** | 0.1f | `[0.05 - 0.2]` |
| **3rd** | 0.16f | `[0.1 - 0.3]` |
| **4th** | 0.26f | `[0.15 - 0.4]` |
| **5th** | 0.41f | `[0.25 - 0.55]` |
| **6th** | 0.66f | `[0.5 - 0.85]` |
| **7th** | 1.0f | Fixed (Always guarantees a match) |

We use **Bayesian Optimization** to efficiently explore these **parameters** and find the best configuration.

### **2. Bayesian Optimization Approach**

Bayesian Optimization will:

1. **Select an initial set of pity mechanic settings** and simulate win rates.
2. **Use Gaussian Processes (GPs)** to predict the best parameters for the next simulation.
3. **Iteratively refine the parameters** to find the optimal pity settings.

#### **Objective Function**

The **objective function minimizes the absolute difference** from the **target win rate per level**:

total_loss = \\sum |Simulated Win Rate - Base Win Rate of Level| / 15

Lower values are better.

---

## **4. Implementing Bayesian Optimization in Python**

```python
import numpy as np
import skopt
from skopt import gp_minimize
from skopt.space import Real
from skopt.utils import use_named_args
import pandas as pd
import random
# Define the optimization space for pity probabilities
param_space = [
    Real(0.05, 0.2, name="pity_2"),   # Pity for 2nd draw
    Real(0.1, 0.3, name="pity_3"),    # Pity for 3rd draw
    Real(0.15, 0.4, name="pity_4"),   # Pity for 4th draw
    Real(0.25, 0.55, name="pity_5"),  # Pity for 5th draw
    Real(0.5, 0.85, name="pity_6")    # Pity for 6th draw
]
# Fixed values for 1st and 7th draws
FIXED_PITY_VALUES = [0.0, 1.0]
# Simulated bot play function
def simulate_pity_mechanic(pity_rates, num_simulations=500):
    win_count = 0
    for _ in range(num_simulations):
        pulls = 0
        while pulls < 7:
            if random.random() < pity_rates[pulls]:
                win_count += 1
                break
            pulls += 1
    return win_count / num_simulations  # Return win rate percentage
# Load base win rates per level (assumed calculated separately)
base_win_rates = {level: random.uniform(40, 60) for level in range(1, 16)}  # Simulated base win rates
@use_named_args(param_space)
def objective(**params):
    pity_rates = [FIXED_PITY_VALUES[0]] + [params[f"pity_{i}"] for i in range(2, 7)] + [FIXED_PITY_VALUES[1]]
    total_loss = 0
    for level in range(1, 16):
        win_rate = simulate_pity_mechanic(pity_rates)
        target_win_rate = base_win_rates[level]
        total_loss += abs(win_rate * 100 - target_win_rate)
    return total_loss / 15
result = gp_minimize(objective, param_space, n_calls=20, random_state=42)
best_pity_values = [FIXED_PITY_VALUES[0]] + result.x + [FIXED_PITY_VALUES[1]]
import ace_tools as tools
optimized_results = pd.DataFrame({
    "Pull Number": list(range(1, 8)),
    "Optimized Pity Probability": best_pity_values
})
tools.display_dataframe_to_user(name="Optimized Pity Mechanic Parameters", dataframe=optimized_results)

null, "identifier": "ART-609", "number": 609, "title": "Various 3D objects that can be dropped on the game board", "description": "The list of objects are under the "3D" section in the GDD, but they are copy pasted here for convenience and tracking purpose.

- [X] Oval Shaped Tiles - These are the only objects that players can drop in the entire game, any other objects are dropped or spawned onto the board by chance, or they appear through a user-initiated power-up.
- [X] Jumbo Tiles - These are large size tiles with 4 icons on them, the moment they hit the platform, the entire game board will shake, possibly sending objects into various pits.
- [X] Hero Tokens - These are the same as the main game, a material required for users to upgrade their character levels. They spawn by chance or appear as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Gold Tiles - These are the same as the main game, a tile that can be saved in a player’s inventory that can be used in the main Dominoes Delights game, they also appear by chance or as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Bomb Tiles - These spawn by % chance, the % chance is tweakable through hero levels from the main game. When a fire token is pushed into the bottom pit, a random bomb tile on the board explodes, blowing nearby pieces in all directions.
- [X] Fire Tokens - These spawn randomly whenever a bomb tile spawns. Bomb tiles and fire tokens effectively spawn as a pair on the board. When they are pushed into the bottom pit, they ignite a bomb tile on the game board.
- [X] Jumbo Tile Token - These are a token representation of the jumbo tile. When they are collected in the bottom pit, an actual jumbo tile will drop onto the board at the tile drop area. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Tile Shower Token - These are a token representation of the tile shower power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a tile shower happens. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Castle Walls Token - These are a token representation of the castle walls power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a pair of castle walls rises for a brief period on the left and right pit of the game board. The duration of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Gems - Hard currency of the game, appears by chance.

null, "identifier": "ART-609", "number": 609, "title": "Various 3D objects that can be dropped on the game board", "description": "The list of objects are under the "3D" section in the GDD, but they are copy pasted here for convenience and tracking purpose.

- [X] Oval Shaped Tiles - These are the only objects that players can drop in the entire game, any other objects are dropped or spawned onto the board by chance, or they appear through a user-initiated power-up.
- [X] Jumbo Tiles - These are large size tiles with 4 icons on them, the moment they hit the platform, the entire game board will shake, possibly sending objects into various pits.
- [X] Hero Tokens - These are the same as the main game, a material required for users to upgrade their character levels. They spawn by chance or appear as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Gold Tiles - These are the same as the main game, a tile that can be saved in a player’s inventory that can be used in the main Dominoes Delights game, they also appear by chance or as a result of a triggered event from the main Dominoes Delights game.
- [X] Bomb Tiles - These spawn by % chance, the % chance is tweakable through hero levels from the main game. When a fire token is pushed into the bottom pit, a random bomb tile on the board explodes, blowing nearby pieces in all directions.
- [X] Fire Tokens - These spawn randomly whenever a bomb tile spawns. Bomb tiles and fire tokens effectively spawn as a pair on the board. When they are pushed into the bottom pit, they ignite a bomb tile on the game board.
- [X] Jumbo Tile Token - These are a token representation of the jumbo tile. When they are collected in the bottom pit, an actual jumbo tile will drop onto the board at the tile drop area. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Tile Shower Token - These are a token representation of the tile shower power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a tile shower happens. The potency of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Castle Walls Token - These are a token representation of the castle walls power-up. When they are collected in the bottom pit, a pair of castle walls rises for a brief period on the left and right pit of the game board. The duration of this effect depends on certain hero levels from the main game.
- [X] Gems - Hard currency of the game, appears by chance.
- [X] Stars - Upgrading currency of the game, appears by chance.
- [ ] New Circular Tokens - These are the main tokens used in Plinko and tile dozer, purple on both sides.", "priority": 2, "estimate": null, "due_date": null, "started_at": null, "completed_at": "2024-08-19T16:23:32Z", "canceled_at": null, "archived_at": null, "time_in_status_minutes": 782111, "labels": ["Sprint 19 - June 14th", "CONCEPT", "Mini Game"], "links": [], "relations": [], "is_archived": false, "created_at": "2024-06-06T21:29:39Z", "updated_at": "2024-08-19T16:23:32Z"}, {"id": "ART-639", "project_id": "1061a4f4-bc6a-45ca-a5b6-7f73d5e0abe2", "team_id": "team_ART", "parent_id": "ENG-1119", "assignee_id": "usr_7fe31e7ec8199618", "creator_id": "usr_Robert", "state_id": "Done", "cycle_id": null, "identifier": "ART-639", "number": 639, "title": "Domino Chest Art", "description": "We need a 3D model of a domino chest, this can be just a repurposed chest we have for the quests, but with the gauge bar on it.

To fine-tune the difficulty system in _Domino Delights_, we are using a *four-stage Bayesian Optimization process*. This ensures that the game maintains *balanced difficulty* while achieving *desired win rates (90%, 75%, 60%, 45%, 30%)* with a *5% margin of error*.

*Optimization Rounds*
*Round 1: Base Pity Mechanic (1st - 7th Pull)*
• *Goal:* Find the optimal *base pity mechanic* values to ensure a balanced win rate across levels.
• *Approach:* Bayesian Optimization tunes *pity activation probabilities per draw* while using the *baseline win rate of each level as the target*.
*Round 2: Adaptive Difficulty Parameters*
• *Goal:* Optimize how the game *dynamically adjusts* based on *hand tiles left, board tiles left, retry count averages*.
• *Approach:* Bayesian Optimization refines the *adaptive pity mechanics* to prevent overcompensation while maintaining a *near-miss experience*.
*Round 3: Pre-Level Puzzle Generation Parameters*
• *Goal:* Optimize *pre-level conditions* to match *target win rates*.
• *Approach:* Bayesian Optimization adjusts:
    ◦ *Win Streak Adjustments (Chops-based bonuses).*
    ◦ *Pre-Level Boosters (Extra tiles & wild tiles).*
    ◦ *Player Bucketing (Hand tile reductions based on past performance).*
    ◦ *Character Level Scaling (Chops-based adjustments).*
    ◦ *Retry-Based Adjustments (Symbol count reductions).*
*Round 4: Final Optimization for Hand Tiles & Chops*
• *Goal:* *Determine the optimal number of hand tiles and chops* to achieve the *target win rate*.
• *Approach:* Using the *optimized parameters from Rounds 1-3*, Bayesian Optimization fine-tunes *hand tiles and chops count* to maintain the expected difficulty balance.
*Why Bayesian Optimization?*
• *Win rates are not deterministic*, requiring a *probabilistic approach*.
• *Difficulty parameters are continuous and interdependent*, making it a *multivariate optimization problem*.
• *Bayesian models efficiently explore the parameter space*, ensuring we find the best configuration *without exhaustive brute-force testing*.
